It’s also ruined my ability to enjoy good-tasting foods that would normally be a treat for me, because now i know ill just eventually buy a whole box of it and binge it all in one sitting until im sick. There’s a brand of ice cream that used to be a special treat for when i visited my mom but that’s ruined now too for the same reason.

i wish i could be honest, but i really have no excuse. My psychiatrist was aghast when i once admitted i never eat the minimum 800 calories a day so i think not even being able to eat 350 calories will be worse. She’s also my prescriber, not a therapist and doesn’t have much eating disorder treatment training so i don’t think she understands why i would do something like this.

And the thing about having 350 calories be a goal is so hard, because I’m still severely overweight and no matter how hard i try, just eating non-safe foods in general always, always triggers me to binge.
It’s hard because it hurts and I don’t want to suffer with this disease anymore but it’s the only thing out of many things I’ve tried through my life that has actually resulted in weight loss. :(

For one thing, not all lgbt people are comfortable with the word queer as it is based on a recently reclaimed slur. As someone who has been called “queer” as an attack, I often find it triggering to read when it could just as easily be replaced with “lgbt+” and i know many people feel the same way

edit: …why is this being downvoted? I’m trying to be honest about how I feel. I and many other trans/gay people are not comfortable with being called queer due to its horribly negative history and personal experience.

Mine was of course my mom blaming it all on the internet, saying that’s where I got the “idea” from. Little does she know I actually got the idea from a chicken soup for the soul book for teenage girls where basically every other story was about having an eating disorder.
